title: Nvidia CEO: Stop Using AI as Your Lazy Excuse for Layoffs
metaDescription: Jensen Huang called out CEOs blaming AI for cuts. The real opportunity? Workers who actually figure out AI tools.
author: Marty @ CertFlo

sections.heading: Jensen Huang Just Called Out Bad CEOs
sections.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang just said what a lot of us already knew. Executives blaming layoffs on AI are giving a "lazy" excuse. According to Business Insider, Huang thinks some leaders use AI as a scapegoat "to sound smart" when they're cutting jobs. This matters cause the dude building the tech powering all this AI stuff is telling us the real story. Companies aren't cutting jobs because AI is taking over. They're cutting jobs cause they don't know what they're doing.

sections.heading: What This Actually Means for You
sections.body:
Here's what Huang's statement really shows: AI isn't the problem. Bad management is. The companies that figured out AI aren't firing people — they're making their people more valuable.

Smart workers already know this. They're not sitting around waiting. They're diving into AI tools and finding something interesting: AI doesn't replace you. It makes you better.

The gap is getting wider fast. Some people are worried about being replaced. Others are learning to prompt ChatGPT, automate stuff with Zapier, and build custom GPTs. They're becoming the employees every company wants to keep.

sections.heading: The Real AI Thing
sections.body:
Those executives Huang called out are missing it entirely. AI isn't about cutting costs through layoffs. It's about making humans do things they couldn't do before. Companies that get this right are seeing workers deliver 10x results.

Think about it: Would you rather be the person who needs replacing or the one using AI to do stuff that seems impossible? Pretty obvious choice. But here's the thing — this window won't stay open forever.

Every month you wait, more people around you are building AI skills. The future isn't humans versus machines. It's AI-powered humans versus everyone else. Which side you gonna be on?

sections.heading: Your Move
sections.body: Jensen Huang just gave you a roadmap. While lazy executives make excuses, people who figured it out build advantages. The AI thing isn't coming — it's here. The question isn't whether AI will change your industry. The question is whether you'll be ahead or scrambling to catch up. The smartest people in your field are already learning. They're building AI workflows, figuring out prompts, and automating the boring stuff. They're not just keeping their jobs — they're creating new ones. If you're ready to actually do something about it, starting with practical AI stuff might be worth looking at.
